items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: A two-channel discrete causal experiment with a public overlap floor. The covariate alphabet is \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\) with known \(d\ge2\), treatment \(A\in\{0,1\}\) and outcome \(Y\in\{0,1\}\), so a complete record \((X,A,Y)\) takes values in \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\). A law \(P\) on this space has covariate masses \(p_j(P)=P(X=j)\), arm masses \(s_{aj}(P)=P(X=j,A=a)\), outcome-marked masses \(q_{aj}(P)=P(X=j,A=a,Y=1)\), propensities \(e_j(P)=s_{1j}(P)/p_j(P)\) on occupied cells, outcome regressions \(\mu_{aj}(P)=q_{aj}(P)/s_{aj}(P)\) (zero on null arm-cells), treatment--covariate marginal \(P_{XA}\), and target \(\tau(P)=\sum_{j=1}^{d}p_j(P)\{\mu_{1j}(P)-\mu_{0j}(P)\}\in[-1,1]\). For a public floor \(\epsilon\in(0,1/4]\), the class \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) consists of the laws with \(e_j(P)\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\) on every occupied cell; no minimum covariate or arm mass is imposed, and null cells and deterministic outcomes are allowed. The data are \(\mathcal D=(\mathcal L,\mathcal V)\sim P^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{XA}^{\otimes m}\) with \(n\ge1\) ordered complete records and \(m\ge0\) ordered treatment--covariate records, together with an independent seed \(U\sim\mathrm{Uniform}[0,1]\). A rule \(T\) is a Borel map of \((\mathcal D,U)\) into \([-1,1]\), and the minimax risk is \(R(n,m,d,\epsilon)=\inf_T\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}\mathbb E[(T(\mathcal D,U)-\tau(P))^2]\). With \(N=n+m\), \(S=n\epsilon\) and \(\ell=\log(\exp(1)+S)\), the comparison functions are \(r(n,m,d,\epsilon)=\min\{1,S^{-1}+(d/(N\epsilon\ell))^2\}\), \(b(n,\epsilon)=\min\{1,(n\epsilon)^{-1}\}\) and \(f(n,m,d)=\min\{1,n^{-1}+d^2/[(n+m)^2\log^2(\exp(1)n)]\}\). The explicit data-only rules are the arm-localized polynomial estimator \(\widehat\tau\) and the inverse-count baseline \(T^{\mathrm B}\); lower bounds use two priors \(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) on complete-record tables and, in the rare-label regime, a two-point pair of amplitude \(\delta\in(0,1/8]\). Comparison constants \(c,C\in(0,\infty)\) are numerical and independent of \((n,m,d,\epsilon)\).

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: A finite potential-outcome overlay on the same discrete world. An extension \(H\) is a law of \((X,A,Y,Y_0,Y_1)\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^4\) whose \((X,A,Y)\)-marginal is \(P\), with binary potential outcomes \(Y_0,Y_1\). It is compatible when \(Y=AY_1+(1-A)Y_0\) holds \(H\)-almost surely and \((Y_0,Y_1)\perp\!\!\!\perp A\mid X\) under \(H\). Causal expectations \(\mathbb E_H[Y_1-Y_0]\) are quantified over compatible extensions only; compatibility restricts the extension and not the observable law.

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl: The exact-marginal benchmark experiment. A side-information rule \(T^{\mathrm K}\) is a Borel map of the \(n\) complete records, the supplied exact table \(P_{XA}\in[0,1]^{2d}\), and an independent \(U\sim\mathrm{Uniform}[0,1]\), into \([-1,1]\); the benchmark risk is \(R^{\mathrm K}(n,d,\epsilon)=\inf_{T^{\mathrm K}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes\mathrm{Uniform}[0,1]}[(T^{\mathrm K}(\mathcal L,P_{XA},U)-\tau(P))^2]\).

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl: Sequences of public experiments. A sequence \(\mathbf v=((n_k,m_k,d_k,\epsilon_k))_{k\ge1}\) takes values in \(\mathbb N_{\ge1}\times\mathbb N_0\times\mathbb N_{\ge2}\times(0,1/4]\) and is otherwise arbitrary (no monotonicity). The consistency phase \(\mathcal C\), the rare-label oracle-order phase \(\mathcal O\) and the strict auxiliary-improvement phase \(\mathcal I\) are sets of such sequences defined through the limiting behaviour of \(R(n_k,m_k,d_k,\epsilon_k)\) as \(k\to\infty\).

items.label: Definition P-1
items.nl: For each \(d\ge2\) and \(0<\epsilon\le1/4\), \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}=\{P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2): P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:overlap}\}\). This is model (3) of Zeng et al., restricted only to the stated range of the public floor.

items.label: Definition P-3
items.nl: \(R(n,m,d,\epsilon)=\inf_T\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{XA}^{\otimes m}\otimes\mathrm{Uniform}[0,1]}[(T(\mathcal D,U)-\tau(P))^2]\). The infimum ranges over all original-record Borel rules, including independent randomized rules; squared-error clipping permits the indicated range.

items.label: Definition P-4
items.nl:
Set \(N=n+m\), \(S=n\epsilon\), and \(\ell=\log(\exp(1)+S)\). The evaluated function is
\[
r(n,m,d,\epsilon)=\min\left\{1,\frac1S+\left(\frac d{N\epsilon\ell}\right)^2\right\}.
\]
All denominators are strictly positive on the public index range. This definition names a positive numerical function; its comparison with the original-experiment minimax risk is the assertion of the frontier theorem.

items.label: Definition P-5
items.nl:
Let \(S=n\epsilon\). If \(S<\exp(4096)\), set \(\widehat\tau(\mathcal D,U)=0\). Otherwise put
\[
\begin{aligned}
h_0&=\lfloor n/3\rfloor,& h_p&=\lfloor(n-h_0)/2\rfloor,& h_f&=n-h_0-h_p,\\
M_p&=h_p+\lfloor m/2\rfloor,&M_f&=h_f+m-\lfloor m/2\rfloor,\\
u&=h_0/8,&t_p&=M_p/8,&t&=M_f/8,\\
L&=\lfloor\log S/1024\rfloor,&B&=2^{20}L/\min\{t_p,t\},&k_0&=\lfloor t_pB/4\rfloor.
\end{aligned}
\]
Use the first \(h_0\) complete records as the outcome pool. Concatenate the treatment--covariate projections of the next \(h_p\) complete records with the first \(\lfloor m/2\rfloor\) auxiliary records as the pilot pool. Concatenate the remaining projections and auxiliary records as the factorial pool. Within each pool retain this ordering. Define
\[
T_0(x)=1,\quad T_1(x)=x,\quad T_{h+1}(x)=2xT_h(x)-T_{h-1}(x),\qquad
E_L(z)=\frac{1-T_L(1-2z)}{2L^2z},\quad
G_L(z)=\frac{1-E_L(z)}z=\sum_{h=0}^{L-2}g_hz^h,
\]
where removable values are used at zero.

For each prefix triple \((h',h'',h''')\) with \(0\le h'\le h_0\), \(0\le h''\le M_p\), \(0\le h'''\le M_f\), let \(Z_{aj}\) count outcome successes in arm \(a\), cell \(j\), in the outcome prefix; let \(J_{aj}\) and \(K_{aj}\) count that arm and cell in the pilot and factorial prefixes. Write \((x)_0=1\) and \((x)_h=x(x-1)\cdots(x-h+1)\) for integer counts, and set
\[
\widehat G_{aj}=\sum_{h=0}^{L-2}g_h\frac{(K_{aj})_h}{(tB)^h},\qquad
P_{aj}^{\mathrm{pol}}=\frac{Z_{aj}}u\left(1+\frac{K_{1-a,j}\widehat G_{aj}}{tB}\right),\qquad
H_{aj}=\frac{Z_{aj}}u\left(1+\frac{K_{1-a,j}}{K_{aj}+1}\right),
\]
\[
V_{aj}=\mathbf1\{J_{aj}\le k_0\}P_{aj}^{\mathrm{pol}}+\mathbf1\{J_{aj}>k_0\}H_{aj},\qquad
F(h',h'',h''';\mathcal D)=\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}\left(\sum_{j=1}^d(V_{1j}-V_{0j})\right).
\]
The total rule, independent of \(U\), is the finite sum
\[
\widehat\tau(\mathcal D,U)=
\sum_{h'=0}^{h_0}\sum_{h''=0}^{M_p}\sum_{h'''=0}^{M_f}
 \exp(-u-t_p-t)\frac{u^{h'}}{h'!}\frac{t_p^{h''}}{h''!}\frac{t^{h'''}}{h'''!}
 F(h',h'',h''';\mathcal D).
\]
The omitted Poisson overflow combinations have output zero. Every division is by a strictly positive public number or by an integer plus one, including on empty observed cells. The construction uses no unknown population probabilities.

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl:
Put \(S=n\epsilon\), \(\ell=\log(\exp(1)+S)\), \(N=n+m\), and \(x=d/(N\epsilon\ell)\). If \(S<\exp(4096)\) or \(x^2\le S^{-1}\), use the two Dirac priors on the two tables in the rare-label theorem, with \(\delta=(16\sqrt{\max\{1,S\}})^{-1}\). Otherwise set
\[
u=128n,\quad w=128N,\quad M=u+w,\quad L=\lceil8\ell\rceil,\quad
B=\frac L{1000M},\quad\alpha=\frac B{100L^2},\quad
b_0=\frac\alpha\epsilon,\quad K_* =\min\{d-1,\lfloor(100b_0)^{-1}\rfloor\}.
\]
Choose a finite dual measure \(\sigma\) from the shrinking-cone dual lemma for these \(L,B,\epsilon\); equivalently use the normalized alternating interpolation weights at \(L+2\) alternation points of a best degree-\(L\) uniform approximant to \(\alpha/(\alpha+(1-\epsilon)v)\), oriented to have nonnegative integral of this function. Define the raw mass functions
\[
w_*(v)=b_0+v,\qquad S_1(v)=\alpha+(1-\epsilon)v,\qquad
S_0(v)=(1-\epsilon)b_0+\epsilon v\qquad(0\le v\le B).
\]
Let \(h(v)\in\{-1,1\}\) be the polar sign of \(\sigma\) at its atoms. Draw each rare-cell latent pair independently with core branch measure \((\alpha/S_1(v))|\sigma|(dv)\), and filler branch at \(v=0\) with remaining probability \(1-\int(\alpha/S_1(v))|\sigma|(dv)\). The branch flag is retained even when the core also has an atom at zero. Under prior \(\Pi_1\), assign treated mean \((1+h(v))/2\) on the core; under \(\Pi_0\), assign \((1-h(v))/2\) there. On the filler use treated mean zero under both priors. Use control mean zero everywhere. The raw treatment--covariate masses are \(S_1(v),S_0(v)\) under both priors.

Use \(K_*\) such rare cells. Let \(\bar w=\mathbb E w_*(V)\) under this common latent marginal and append a reservoir cell of raw covariate mass \(p_*=1-K_*\bar w\), propensity \(1/2\), and both outcome means zero. Set the remaining cells null. Finally set \(Q=p_*+\sum_{i=1}^{K_*}w_*(V_i)\) and divide every raw complete-record probability by \(Q\). The two priors are the pushforwards of these finite product distributions to the resulting complete-record tables. Membership, positivity of the reservoir and normalizer, target separation, and joint likelihood bounds are conclusions proved in the affine-testing lemma, not premises built into this construction.

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl: \(R^{\mathrm K}(n,d,\epsilon)=\inf_{T^{\mathrm K}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes\mathrm{Uniform}[0,1]}[(T^{\mathrm K}(\mathcal L,P_{XA},U)-\tau(P))^2]\), where \(\mathcal L\) is the complete-record component of \(\mathcal D\).

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl: Define \(T^{\mathrm B}=0\) if \(n<6\). Otherwise use the first \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor\) complete records as an outcome pool and concatenate the remaining treatment--covariate projections with all auxiliary records as a marginal pool. Draw independent Poisson prefixes with means one eighth of their pool sizes; output zero on overflow. For valid prefixes, for each \((a,j)\) multiply its outcome-success count divided by the outcome-prefix mean by one plus the opposite-arm marginal count divided by one plus its own-arm marginal count. Sum treated contributions minus control contributions, clip to \([-1,1]\), and average over all finitely many valid prefix lengths with their known Poisson probabilities; invalid prefixes contribute zero.

items.label: Definition P-9
items.nl: \(\mathcal C=\{\mathbf v: R(n_k,m_k,d_k,\epsilon_k)\to0\}\), \(\mathcal O=\{\mathbf v: n_k\epsilon_k\to\infty,\ \limsup_{k\to\infty}R(n_k,m_k,d_k,\epsilon_k)/b(n_k,\epsilon_k)<\infty\}\), and \(\mathcal I=\{\mathbf v: R(n_k,m_k,d_k,\epsilon_k)/R(n_k,0,d_k,\epsilon_k)\to0\}\). Each set ranges over every allowed sequence \(\mathbf v=((n_k,m_k,d_k,\epsilon_k))_{k\ge1}\).

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl:
For probability measures \(
u,
u'\) on a finite set, with natural logarithms in the Kullback--Leibler divergence, \(\operatorname{TV}(
u,
u')\le\sqrt{D(
u\Vert
u')/2}\), where \(\operatorname{TV}(
u,
u')= rac12\sum_z|
u(z)-
u'(z)|\).

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl: For a real polynomial \(g\) of degree at most \(L\) on \([-1,1]\), \(\|g'\|_\infty\le L^2\|g\|_\infty\).

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl:
Let \(g\) be continuous on a nondegenerate compact interval \([v_-,v_+]\), and let \(L\ge0\) be an integer. There is a finite signed measure \(\sigma\), supported on at most \(L+2\) points, such that \(\|\sigma\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=1\), \(\int v^h\,d\sigma(v)=0\) for \(0\le h\le L\), and
\[
\int g\,d\sigma=\inf_{Q:\deg Q\le L}\sup_{v\in[v_-,v_+]}|g(v)-Q(v)|.
\]
Here \(\|\sigma\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\) denotes the total mass of its variation measure, rather than the distance between two probabilities.

items.label: Lemma L-4
items.nl:
For \(K\sim\operatorname{Poi}(\lambda)\), \(\lambda\ge0\), let \(g(K)=1/(K+1)\). With \(C_0=2^{16}\),
\[
\mathbb E g(K)=\begin{cases}(1-e^{-\lambda})/\lambda,&\lambda>0,\\1,&\lambda=0,\end{cases}\qquad
\mathbb E g(K)^2\le\frac{C_0}{(1+\lambda)^2},\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(g(K))\le\frac{C_0\lambda}{(1+\lambda)^4}.
\]

items.label: Lemma L-5
items.nl:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\), an arm \(a\), and positive intensities \(u,t\). In two independent Poisson pools let the outcome-success counts \(Z_j\) have means \(u q_{aj}(P)\), and the marginal arm counts \(K_j,W_j\) have means \(t s_{aj}(P),t s_{1-a,j}(P)\). All counts in this display are independent across cells and pools, and the two marginal arm counts are independent. Define
\[
H_j=\frac{Z_j}{u}\left(1+\frac{W_j}{K_j+1}\right),\qquad \psi_a=\sum_{j=1}^d p_j(P)\mu_{aj}(P).
\]
There is a numerical \(C\) such that
\[
\left|\mathbb E\sum_jH_j-\psi_a\right|\le\min\left\{1,\frac{d}{\exp(1)t\epsilon}\right\},\qquad
\operatorname{Var}\left(\sum_jH_j\right)\le C\left(\frac1{u\epsilon}+\frac1{t\epsilon}\right).
\]

items.label: Lemma L-6
items.nl: Consider finitely many independent ordered iid pools of lengths \(h_i\ge1\), and independent prefix lengths \(J_i\sim\operatorname{Poi}(h_i/8)\). Let a statistic of the corresponding infinite iid prefixes take values in \([-1,1]\), with mean squared error at most \(A\) for a target \(\vartheta\in[-1,1]\). Replace its output by zero whenever some \(J_i>h_i\), and conditionally average over the prefix lengths given the finite pools. The resulting finite sum is a total deterministic Borel rule with risk at most \(A+\sum_i e^{-h_i}\).

items.label: Lemma L-7
items.nl:
For an integer \(L\ge2\), let \(C_L(z)=T_L(1-2z)\), where \(T_0(x)=1\), \(T_1(x)=x\), and \(T_{h+1}(x)=2xT_h(x)-T_{h-1}(x)\). Define the polynomials
\[
E_L(z)=\frac{1-C_L(z)}{2L^2z},\qquad G_L(z)=\frac{1-E_L(z)}z=\sum_{h=0}^{L-2}g_hz^h
\]
by their removable values at zero. Then \(0\le E_L(z)\le\min\{1,(L^2z)^{-1}\}\) for \(0<z\le1\), \(E_L(0)=1\), and \(\sum_h|g_h|\le14^L\). If \(K\sim\operatorname{Poi}(tzB)\), \(t,B>0\), \(D=tB\ge L\), and
\[
\widehat G=\sum_{h=0}^{L-2}g_h\frac{(K)_h}{D^h},\qquad (K)_0=1,\quad (K)_h=K(K-1)\cdots(K-h+1),
\]
then \(\mathbb E\widehat G=G_L(z)\) and \(\mathbb E\widehat G^2\le392^L(1+z)^{2L}\) for every \(z\ge0\).

items.label: Lemma L-8
items.nl:
Fix an allowed experiment with \(S=n\epsilon\ge\exp(4096)\), put \(L=\lfloor\log S/1024\rfloor\), and let \(u\ge n/32\), \(t_p,t\ge N/64\), with \(1/3\le t/t_p\le3\). Put \(H_0=2^{20}\), \(B=H_0L/\min\{t_p,t\}\), and \(k_0=\lfloor t_pB/4\rfloor\). For \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) and a fixed arm \(a\), use independent Poisson outcome, pilot and factorial pools with these intensities, and form \(V_{aj}\) by the formulas of the estimator construction. Then
\[
\mathbb E\left(\sum_{j=1}^dV_{aj}-\sum_{j=1}^d p_j(P)\mu_{aj}(P)\right)^2
\le C\left\{\frac1S+\left(\frac d{N\epsilon L}\right)^2\right\}
\]
for a numerical \(C\) independent of every public index and of the law.

items.label: Lemma L-9
items.nl:
For \(L\ge2\), \(B>0\), \(0<\epsilon\le1/4\), and \(\alpha=B/(100L^2)\), there is a finite signed measure \(\sigma\) on \([0,B]\), supported on at most \(L+2\) points, with \(\|\sigma\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=1\), \(\int v^h\,d\sigma=0\) for \(0\le h\le L\), and
\[
\int\frac{\alpha}{\alpha+(1-\epsilon)v}\,d\sigma(v)\ge\frac18.
\]

items.label: Lemma L-10
items.nl:
For allowed public indices put \(S=n\epsilon\), \(N=n+m\), \(\ell=\log(\exp(1)+S)\), and \(x=d/(N\epsilon\ell)\). If \(S\ge\exp(4096)\) and \(x^2>S^{-1}\), the affine priors in the prior construction are supported on \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\), have exactly the same distribution of the normalized \(P_{XA}\), and prove
\[
R(n,m,d,\epsilon)\ge c\min\{1,x^2\}
\]
for a strictly positive numerical \(c\). The inequality holds against all randomized Borel rules in the original fixed-size two-channel experiment.

items.label: Lemma L-11
items.nl:
Every \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) admits a potential-outcome extension \(H\) satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:exchangeability}\). Call precisely these extensions compatible. For every compatible extension,
\[
\mathbb E_H[Y_1-Y_0]=\tau(P).
\]
Conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes with means \(\mu_{0j}(P),\mu_{1j}(P)\), independent of treatment given \(X=j\), followed by \(Y=Y_A\), give one compatible extension. This is an existence witness; the universal identifying equality requires no independence between the potential outcomes.

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: There is a numerical constant \(c>0\), independent of all public indices, such that \(R(n,m,d,\epsilon)\ge c\,b(n,\epsilon)\) for every allowed \((n,m,d,\epsilon)\). The same bound holds for \(R^{\mathrm K}(n,d,\epsilon)\). A legal pair uses \(p_1=p_2=1/2\), \(e_1=e_2=\epsilon\), \(\mu_{01}=\mu_{02}=1/2\), and \(\mu_{11}=\mu_{12}=1/2\pm\delta\), with other cells null. Its auxiliary laws coincide, its targets are \(\pm\delta\), and its one-record Kullback--Leibler divergence at \(\delta=1/8\) equals \(\epsilon\log(5/3)/4\). The lower bound ranges over every original-record randomized Borel rule.

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl: There is a numerical constant \(C<\infty\), independent of \((n,m,d,\epsilon)\), such that the total rule \(T^{\mathrm B}\) satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}\mathbb E[(T^{\mathrm B}(\mathcal D)-\tau(P))^2]\le C\min\{1,(n\epsilon)^{-1}+[d/((n+m)\epsilon)]^2\}\) for every allowed experiment. Boundary Bernoulli outcomes and null cells are included.

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon\le1/4\), the evaluated function of \(\mathrm{def:rate\mbox{-}handle}\) satisfies
\[
r(n,m,d,\epsilon)\asymp_{\epsilon}f(n,m,d)
\]
uniformly in \(n,m,d\), recovering the fixed-overlap annotation benchmark. In the same observable class,
\[
R(n,m,2,\epsilon)\asymp b(n,\epsilon),\qquad
R^{\mathrm K}(n,d,\epsilon)\asymp b(n,\epsilon),
\]
with numerical comparison constants independent of every public index. For every allowed \((n,d,\epsilon)\) and every \(m\ge1\), the actual two-channel and exact-marginal minimax risks satisfy the finite-sample experiment comparison
\[
0\le R(n,m,d,\epsilon)-R^{\mathrm K}(n,d,\epsilon)
\le\min\left\{1,6(n+2)\sqrt{\frac{2d}{m}}\right\}.
\]
Consequently, with \((n,d,\epsilon)\) fixed,
\[
\lim_{m\to\infty}R(n,m,d,\epsilon)=R^{\mathrm K}(n,d,\epsilon).
\]
For every finite \(M_0>0\), all allowed experiments with \(n\epsilon\le M_0\) have risk bounded below by a strictly positive number depending only on \(M_0\), regardless of the auxiliary budget. These results include null cells and boundary Bernoulli laws. No interchange of the fixed-parameter limit with a vanishing overlap floor is asserted.

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl:
Set \(N=n+m\), \(S=n\epsilon\), \(\ell=\log(\exp(1)+S)\), and
\[
r(n,m,d,\epsilon)=\min\left\{1,S^{-1}+\left(\frac d{N\epsilon\ell}\right)^2\right\}.
\]
There are numerical constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\), independent of all public indices, such that
\[
c\,r(n,m,d,\epsilon)\le R(n,m,d,\epsilon)
\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}\mathbb E_P(\widehat\tau(\mathcal D,U)-\tau(P))^2
\le C\,r(n,m,d,\epsilon)
\]
for every allowed experiment. Here \(\mathbb E_P\) denotes expectation under \(P^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{XA}^{\otimes m}\otimes\mathrm{Uniform}[0,1]\). The finite prefix-average rule in the estimator construction is an explicit total deterministic Borel attaining estimator. The normalized finite priors in the prior construction furnish the all-procedure lower bound in the actual unequal-channel experiment. In particular the logarithm is governed by rare outcome-label information \(n\epsilon\), while the approximation denominator uses all \((n+m)\epsilon\) marginal information; the comparison is uniform in the public overlap floor, includes null cells and deterministic outcomes, and has no sample-ratio restriction.

The causal interpretation is restricted to compatible extensions: every \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) admits at least one extension \(H\) satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:exchangeability}\), and for every such extension the observable target in this risk comparison satisfies \(\tau(P)=\mathbb E_H[Y_1-Y_0]\).

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl:
For an arbitrary allowed sequence \(\mathbf v=((n_k,m_k,d_k,\epsilon_k))_{k\ge1}\), put \(S_k=n_k\epsilon_k\), \(N_k=n_k+m_k\), and \(\ell_k=\log(\exp(1)+S_k)\). The phases in \(\mathrm{def:phases}\) have the exact characterizations
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf v\in\mathcal C\quad&\Longleftrightarrow\quad
S_k\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad d_k=o(N_k\epsilon_k\ell_k),\\
\mathbf v\in\mathcal O\quad&\Longleftrightarrow\quad
S_k\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad
 d_k=O\left(\frac{N_k\epsilon_k\ell_k}{\sqrt{S_k}}\right),\\
\mathbf v\in\mathcal I\quad&\Longleftrightarrow\quad
S_k\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad
\frac{d_k}{\sqrt{S_k}\ell_k}\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad
\frac{N_k/n_k}{\max\{1,d_k/(S_k\ell_k)\}}\longrightarrow\infty.
\end{aligned}
\]
There is also a universal finite-sample saturation elbow: writing \(N=n+m\), \(S=n\epsilon\), and \(\ell=\log(\exp(1)+S)\),
\[
d\ge N\epsilon\ell\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
R(n,m,d,\epsilon)\asymp1
\]
with numerical comparison constants. Conditional on \(S_k\to\infty\), consistency begins exactly at \(d_k=o(N_k\epsilon_k\ell_k)\).
In the supervised slice \(m_k=0\), consistency is equivalent to \(S_k\to\infty\) and \(d_k=o(S_k\ell_k)\), while oracle order is equivalent to \(S_k\to\infty\) and \(d_k=O(\sqrt{S_k}\ell_k)\); strict auxiliary improvement is empty on that slice. In any sequence with \(S_k\to\infty\), oracle order is reached precisely when the marginal budget satisfies
\[
N_k=\Omega\left(\frac{d_k\sqrt{S_k}}{\epsilon_k\ell_k}\right),\qquad N_k\ge n_k.
\]
Then \(R(n_k,m_k,d_k,\epsilon_k)\asymp S_k^{-1}\), and further increases of auxiliary budgets cannot improve that order. For any single allowed experiment, the order plateau holds with universal comparison constants whenever
\[
N\ge\frac{d\sqrt{n\epsilon}}{\epsilon\log(\exp(1)+n\epsilon)};
\]
the comparison is with the capped benchmark \(b(n,\epsilon)\), including when \(n\epsilon<1\).
